why: The clause that makes the `marks` row replace the leading mark (issue #1022). The row draws this slot's outline once per stock, so a leading copy states the identity a second time -- and lands next to a hollow LOST mark of the same shape. For slot 1 those are the same circle drawn the same way, so an entry that has lost a stock appears to carry two identity marks instead of one and a spent stock. Measured on a real frame before the guard existed (issue #230). Rewritten by #1022 from the `stockCue !== 'marks'` clause it used to drop; the row is now the shipped FFA strip.
killedBy: hud: identity mark in the stock strip (issue #778) draws the leading mark under arcs and roof, and none under shape, whose row replaces it (issue #1022)
hud: identity-shaped stocks, the `marks` arm (issue #230) suppresses the leading marker, which is the whole point of the arm
